title: Opt-in GPU keep-warm between live frames (perception.gpu_keepalive_ms, default off)
hypothesis: If a background thread launches a tiny CUDA kernel every few ms between live frames, the laptop GPU stays in a high power state and the camera CNN at a 0.2 s cadence drops from 55-59 ms toward its back-to-back 3-4 ms, at a measured power cost

eval.benchmark: LabPipeline on 40 real frames paced at 0.25 s, 7 alternating repeats: perception_tracking 138.9 -> 106.8 ms (ranges do not overlap), frame -22%, at +18.6 W (3072/20 ms) or ~+8 W (2048/10 ms); DEFAULT OFF

notes: Hypothesis as stated REFUTED: tiny ops (1-element add, 64-512 matmul, any period 2-20 ms) leave the GPU in P8 (CNN 57-59 ms at a 0.2 s cadence). Only a sustained ~35-40 % load raises clocks: kept as an opt-in power burner (perception.gpu_keepalive_ms/gpu_keepalive_matmul, default 0). The owner's power setting remains the preferred fix. Windows Event.wait ticks at ~15.6 ms; time.sleep is high-resolution.

lessons.text: Laptop NVIDIA GPUs stay in P8 under light periodic load; tiny keep-alive kernels cannot hold clocks, only ~35-40 % sustained load does (measured +8 to +18.6 W)
